title: Quest
description: Innovative robotics project combining a drone with a rover.

content.heading: introduction
content.text: Quest is a multifunctional rescue robot designed to operate efficiently in critical and hard-to-reach environments. Developed by me and Alexandru-Lucian Motoașcă at Colegiul Național de Informatică “Grigore Moisil” Brașov, this project combines ground mobility and aerial versatility to assist in emergency missions such as locating missing persons, exploring caves, or supporting firefighting operations.

content.heading: motivation
content.text: The idea behind Quest emerged from a real need for innovative tools that can save lives in extreme situations. Traditional rescue missions are often delayed or limited by terrain and safety constraints. Quest was imagined as a machine capable of overcoming these obstacles — a robot that can both drive on four wheels and take flight, reaching areas where human access is dangerous or impossible.

content.heading: capabilities & usefulness
content.text: Quest operates in two main modes:
list: Rover mode: Moves on wheels, consumes minimal energy, and can transport small medical kits such as bandages or food to people trapped in hazardous zones.

Drone mode: With a simple command, Quest extends its arms and transforms into a quadcopter, capable of scanning large areas from above. It can detect heat sources, locate survivors, and transmit live video data to emergency teams.
content.subtext: Equipped with a high-resolution camera, AI-based object detection, and real-time image transmission, Quest provides an intelligent and adaptive solution for both monitoring and active intervention.

content.heading: design and structure
content.text: Mechanically, Quest is an elegant fusion of robotics and aeronautics. Its frame is 3D-printed using PETG and PETG-CF, ensuring strength without excessive weight.
list: Each leg integrates two servo motors for articulation.
Each wheel assembly includes a DC motor and a brushless motor with propeller for flight.
Magnetic supports reduce strain on servos and stabilize the robot even when unpowered.
The centrally placed battery ensures balance and easy replacement.

content.heading: electronics and control
content.text: The electronic system integrates multiple components for stability and intelligence:
list: Raspberry Pi 4B – main controller managing overall coordination and communication.
Arduino Mega – controls servo and DC motors.
Pixhawk 2.4.8 – handles flight stabilization and telemetry.
OAK-D Lite – provides real-time vision with object detection using YOLOv8 nano.
content.subtext: The power system uses multiple voltage converters to safely supply all modules, while serial and UART communication links keep sensors, motors, and processors synchronized.

content.heading: Software and AI
list: A Flask-based backend hosted on Raspberry Pi for communication and data routing.
Socket.io for real-time video and telemetry streaming.
Integration with YOLOv8n on OAK-D Lite for object and human detection.
A React-based web interface hosted on Firebase, accessible through a secure ngrok tunnel.
Custom Arduino firmware managing low-level control and safety fallbacks.

content.heading: Future Development
content.text: Quest continues to evolve with potential improvements such as:
list: Higher-capacity batteries for extended missions.
Integration of gas and thermal sensors for hazardous environments.
Machine learning for autonomous navigation and improved object recognition.
Collaborative multi-robot communication for large-scale search missions.

content.heading: Action Demos
content.text: Watch Quest in action as it navigates terrain and demonstrates its dual-mode capabilities.

content.heading: Camera Perspective
content.text: A glimpse through the OAK-D Lite camera, showing the real-time perspective and environmental awareness of the robot.

content.heading: Conclusion
content.text: Quest represents a fusion of creativity, engineering, and purpose — a machine built not just to demonstrate technical ability, but to save lives. Through the combination of robotics, AI, and intelligent control systems, Quest pushes the boundaries of what small-scale autonomous systems can achieve in emergency response.

title: AdReverse AI
description: Autonomous competitor ad reverse-engineering and UGC counter-campaign synthesis studio.

content.heading: introduction
content.text: AdReverse AI is an end-to-end competitive intelligence and counter-advertising engine built during the ITFest Adobe 12-hour Hackathon. Designed for performance marketers and direct-to-consumer (DTC) brands, it automates the traditional weeks-long creative audit into an autonomous, real-time pipeline that deconstructs competitor scaling strategies and generates production-ready counter-campaigns in seconds.
content.subtext: Instead of static spreadsheets, the system crawls live competitor creatives across Meta and TikTok, pinpoints their underlying psychological mechanisms and offer weaknesses, and synthesizes high-converting counter-ads complete with frame-by-frame UGC creator scripts.

content.heading: architecture & monorepo structure
content.text: AdReverse is built as a contract-first monorepo, enforcing strict type safety across both frontend and backend layers via a centralized contracts package in /shared.
content.code:
adreverse/
├── shared/         # Single source of truth: TypeScript data contracts & mock fixtures
│   └── types.ts    # CamelCase interfaces shared across Next.js and FastAPI
├── back/           # Asynchronous Python FastAPI backend
│   ├── app/
│   │   ├── routers/   # REST endpoints (brand, discovery, ads, campaign)
│   │   ├── schemas/   # Pydantic V2 domain models with CamelModel aliases
│   │   └── services/  # AI inference, LangChain orchestrator, Supabase persistence
│   └── main.py     # FastAPI entrypoint
└── front/          # Next.js 16 App Router frontend
    └── src/
        ├── app/        # App Router pages (/ and /dashboard) & Clerk auth
        └── components/ # 4-Step workflow modules (Onboarding, Radar, Analysis, Studio)
content.subtext: By maintaining strict camelCase properties in all Pydantic schemas and TypeScript models, JSON payloads serialize seamlessly between Next.js client components and FastAPI endpoints without manual field translation.

content.heading: the ai pipeline: from live crawl to synthesis
content.text: The core of AdReverse is a reactive, multi-stage AI workflow engineered for low-latency market analysis and high-fidelity creative synthesis. The architecture links live web scraping with parallelized LLM reasoning across four distinct phases:
list: 1. Real-time Ingestion (Jina Reader & Tavily API): When a brand domain is onboarded, Jina Reader (https://r.jina.ai/) strips boilerplate HTML to extract clean markdown, while Tavily Search API runs targeted search queries across live Meta Ad Library and SERP records.

2. Competitor Radar & Market Discovery: Tavily web context is fed into LangChain's structured output model (Pydantic V2), identifying top rivals, market share tiers (dominant, challenger, niche), active channels, and opportunity gaps.

3. Concurrent Ad Deconstruction (asyncio.gather): Active competitor creatives are scraped and processed simultaneously across asynchronous worker pools, deconstructing hooks, emotional triggers, and vulnerability gaps in parallel.

4. Multi-Angle Counter-Campaign Synthesis: Once vulnerabilities are extracted, concurrent LLM workers synthesize three distinct counter-campaign angles (Direct Comparison, Problem Agitation, Social Proof) alongside frame-by-frame UGC storyboards in under 3.5 seconds.

content.heading: competitor radar & market discovery
content.text: The discovery engine continuously scans the target vertical. It retrieves active competitors, quantifies their market share tier, and computes an Estimated Reach Score (0–100%) alongside active media channels across Meta, Instagram, and TikTok.
content.subtext: The platform analyzes cross-channel competitor saturation to uncover blind spots and opportunity gaps before generating ad counter-attacks.

content.heading: concurrent ad scraping & reverse-engineering
content.text: Rather than evaluating ads sequentially, the Ad Breakdown engine uses Python's asyncio.gather to dispatch independent extraction tasks for every creative unit in parallel. Each ad is dissected through a rigorous performance marketing lens:
list: 3-Second Hook Extraction: Identifies whether the opening leverages a bold statement, pattern interrupt, or problem agitation.
Psychological Mechanism: Analyzes how the competitor promises resolution (e.g. proprietary formulations, speed, convenience).
Offer Structure: Parses pricing, bundle incentives, guarantees, or hidden fees.
Vulnerability Gap Mining: Exposes strategic flaws (such as unverified claims, subscription lock-ins, or premium markups) ready for targeted counter-messaging.

content.heading: multi-angle campaign synthesis & ugc storyboards
content.text: Once competitor vulnerabilities are identified, the Campaign Studio synthesizes counter-strategies across three distinct psychological angles concurrently: Direct Comparison, Problem Agitation, and Social Proof.
content.code:
# back/app/services/campaign_service.py
tasks = [
    _generate_angle_campaign(angle)
    for angle in ["direct_comparison", "problem_agitation", "social_proof_reviews"]
]
results = await asyncio.gather(*tasks, return_exceptions=True)

for campaign, strategy in results:
    generated_campaigns.append(campaign)
    adaptation_strategies.append(strategy)
content.subtext: Running angle generation concurrently dropped full campaign synthesis latency from 90+ seconds down to under 3.5 seconds.

content.heading: fault-tolerant tiered inference pipeline
content.text: To guarantee reliability and eliminate downtime during intense hackathon demos or production spikes, AdReverse employs a multi-tier fallback pipeline with LangChain. Requests route first to ultra-low latency Groq models and automatically cascade to Google Gemini if rate limits occur.
content.code:
# back/app/services/ai_service.py
def get_llm():
    primary = ChatGroq(
        model="openai/gpt-oss-20b",
        api_key=settings.GROQ_API_KEY.strip(),
        temperature=0.2,
        timeout=15,
    )
    fallback_models = [
        ChatGroq(model="openai/gpt-oss-120b", timeout=15),
        ChatGroq(model="qwen/qwen3.8-27b", timeout=15),
        ChatGoogleGenerativeAI(model="gemini-3.5-flash-lite", timeout=15),
        ChatGoogleGenerativeAI(model="gemini-3.8-flash", timeout=15),
    ]
    return primary.with_fallbacks(fallback_models)
content.subtext: Primary inference runs on Groq in ~0.3s, cascading down to secondary models and Google Gemini without throwing 500 errors to the client.

content.heading: frame-by-frame ugc storyboard engine
content.text: The final deliverable bridges AI strategy with real-world production. For every campaign angle, the studio generates an actionable UGC storyboard formatted specifically for TikTok and 9:16 Instagram Reels.
content.subtext: Includes precise time-stamps, visual directions, audio scripts, and transition cues, enabling creators to film counter-ads immediately without additional scriptwriting.

content.heading: tech stack
list: Frontend: Next.js 16 (App Router), Turbopack, React 19, Tailwind CSS, Radix UI Primitives, Lucide Icons.
Backend: FastAPI (Python 3.12, fully async), Pydantic V2 with CamelModel serialization.
AI & Orchestration: Groq (ultra-low latency inference), LangChain with multi-cloud fallbacks (Google Gemini), Tavily Search API, Jina Reader.
Database & Auth: Supabase (PostgreSQL with JSONB caching <50ms), Clerk Authentication (Multi-brand vaults & user isolation).

content.heading: conclusion
content.text: Built under the pressure of a 12-hour hackathon at ITFest Adobe, AdReverse AI proves how autonomous multi-agent pipelines and contract-first architecture can democratize competitive intelligence. By bridging raw web crawling, psychological hook deconstruction, and instant creative synthesis, it gives brands an unfair advantage in performance marketing.

title: RippleTrace
description: A Financial GraphRAG engine that predicts and visualizes global supply chain and market risks.

content.heading: overview
content.text: RippleTrace is a specialized Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation (GraphRAG) platform designed to map and quantify 'ripple effects' in global financial markets. It transforms unstructured news and dense regulatory filings into a structured Neo4j Knowledge Graph to uncover non-obvious dependencies.

content.heading: technical architecture
content.text: The system follows a 'Source-to-Graph-to-Inference' pipeline, optimized for low-latency financial intelligence:
list: Data Ingestion: High-throughput crawlers for Alpaca/Yahoo Finance and a specialized SEC 10-K 'Risk Factor' parser via sec-api.
Graph Database: Neo4j acts as the primary source of truth, storing entities and high-dimensional relationships.
Backend Engine: FastAPI with a modern lifespan architecture for efficient database connection pooling.
Frontend: Next.js 15+ application utilizing react-force-graph for interactive supply chain visualization.

content.heading: tiered model strategy
content.text: RippleTrace employs a dual-model approach to balance speed and reasoning depth:
list: Llama 3.1 8B (Instant): Processes real-time news articles, prioritizing high throughput for daily event extraction.
Llama 3.3 70B (Versatile): Leveraged for deep reasoning on SEC 10-K filings, where a large context window and complex entity resolution are required to parse dense legal language.
Groq Inference: All extractions utilize ChatGroq for sub-second LLM response times.

content.heading: knowledge graph ontology
content.text: The system utilizes a custom financial ontology in src/extractor.py, moving beyond simple NER to risk-aware graph extraction:
list: Specialized Entities: Risk_Event (disasters, strikes), Raw_Material, Product, Financial_Metric, and Market_Index.
Directed Relationships: VULNERABLE_TO / EXPOSED_TO (future risk mapping), IMPACTS_METRIC (linkage to quantitative data), and SUPPLIES / DEPENDS_ON (vertical supply chain backbone).
Data Lineage: Every entity is connected to its source via a REPORTS_ON relationship, providing perfect traceability from a graph node back to the original article snippet.

content.heading: graph database visualization
content.text: The extracted knowledge is persisted in a Neo4j instance, enabling complex multi-hop queries to trace risk propagation through the global supply chain.

content.heading: graphrag & traversal logic
content.text: Instead of standard vector search, RippleTrace uses structural graph traversal for deterministic context retrieval:
list: 2-Hop Neighborhoods: The API retrieves subgraphs centered around a ticker, filtering out 'Region' nodes to eliminate network noise while maintaining supply chain context.
Structural Reasoning: The risk-assessment endpoint identifies exact dependency chains (e.g., 'Port Strike' -> 'Semi-conductor Plant' -> 'Tech Ticker') to feed the LLM hallucination-free context.
Path Normalization: Custom Python logic in the API layer handles path reconstruction to ensure data integrity during complex multi-hop Cypher queries.

title: .flux
description: An AI-first engineering intelligence dashboard that gives your code a voice.

content.heading: introduction
content.text: .flux is an engineering intelligence platform designed to centralize the fragmented context of software development. Created by me and Tisca Catalin during the "AI Thinkerers" Hackathon in Bucharest (organized by ElevenLabs), this project secured 4th place in the local competition.
content.subtext: The platform ingests signals from GitHub repositories, pull requests, and voice meetings into a unified Convex database, allowing AI agents to analyze the "pulse" of an engineering team.

content.heading: the problem & solution
content.text: Engineering context is often scattered across code, chat logs, and call notes. AI agents typically act blindly without access to this historical data. .flux solves this by creating a "God mode" context layer. It captures:
list: Code Metadata: PRs, commits, and file changes via GitHub.
Human Context: Voice calls and architectural decisions via ElevenLabs.
Team Dynamics: Contributor roles and seniority inferred from code complexity.

content.heading: agentic workflow
content.text: Unlike simple CI/CD scripts, .flux employs autonomous agents to reason about the data:
list: The Analyst (PRAnalyzer): Proactively monitors PRs to assess risk levels (Low to Critical) and impact radius without human intervention.
The Profiler (ContributorProfiler): Analyzes commit history to infer if a contributor is a "Frontend Junior" or "Backend Lead".
The Scribe (Meeting Listener): Uses ElevenLabs Scribe v1 to Transcribe engineering calls and extract actionable TODOs linked to specific files.

content.heading: voice intelligence
content.text: The crown jewel of the project is the RepoAssistant Agent. It allows engineers to literally "talk" to their codebase. Using ElevenLabs Multilingual v2 for speech-out and the Vercel AI SDK for orchestration, users can ask questions like "What is the risk level of the last 3 PRs?" or "Who owns the payment infrastructure?" and receive a spoken, context-aware answer.

list: Frontend: Next.js 16 (App Dir), React 19, Tailwind CSS v4, Shadcn UI.
Backend & DB: Convex (Real-time database and scheduled functions).
AI & Agents: Vercel AI SDK, OpenAI, ElevenLabs (STT & TTS).
Auth & Tools: Clerk Authentication, Octokit (GitHub API).

content.heading: conclusion
content.text: .flux moves beyond static dashboards. By combining deep code analysis with voice intelligence, it creates a living, breathing interface for software engineering teams. It transforms raw metadata into actionable insights, bridging the gap between what the code says and what the team intends.

title: Udraw
description: C# WinForms Drawing App with SQL Storage.

content.heading: overview
content.text: uDraw is a personal project built in C# (WinForms) to explore the intersection of GUI development, graphics rendering, and SQL database management. The goal: create a simple desktop drawing environment that can save drawings into an SQL Server database and later load them back as editable canvases.

content.heading: application structure
content.code:
uDraw/
├── Forms/
│   ├── MainForm.cs
│   ├── SaveForm.cs
│   └── LoadForm.cs
├── Components/
│   └── PaintingCanvas.cs
├── Database/
│   ├── DatabaseHelper.cs
│   └── DatabaseConfig.cs
├── Properties/
└── Program.cs
content.subtext:
The app follows a clean separation of concerns:
• UI Layer → Forms for user interaction
• Graphics Layer → Canvas rendering
• Persistence Layer → SQL Server CRUD operations

content.heading: drawing logic
content.text: The PaintingCanvas control is the core of uDraw. It captures mouse input, renders strokes, and maintains a Bitmap buffer to avoid flicker.

content.heading: database integration
content.text: Each drawing is stored in SQL Server as a VARBINARY(MAX) column. The DatabaseHelper handles serialization and CRUD operations.

title: AutoMounterShell
description: A shell wrapper for Linux where you can mount and unmount drives without commands.

content.heading: overview
content.text: AMSH (Auto Mount Shell) is a custom command-line interpreter designed for Linux systems to automate the management of storage devices. Developed in collaboration with Iosub Dragoș-Casian, this project focuses on efficiency and resource management by handling the mounting and unmounting of file systems automatically based on user activity.

content.heading: key features
content.text: AMSH enhances the standard shell experience with intelligent background processes:
list: Smart Auto-Mounting: Automatically detects when a user navigates (`cd`) to a mountpoint or accesses files within it, mounting the device instantly.
TTL (Time To Live) Management: Monitors inactivity and automatically unmounts devices after a configurable period to save resources and ensure safety.
Desktop Notifications: Integrates with `notify-send` to alert the user in the GUI when devices are mounted or unmounted.
Custom TUI: Features a stylized ASCII interface, colored prompts showing the current user and path, and formatted history tables.

content.heading: configuration
content.text: The system is highly configurable via the amsh.conf file, allowing users to define specific TTLs (in minutes) and file system types for different devices.
content.code:
# DEVICE            MOUNTPOINT                FS_TYPE   TTL
/tmp/disk.img       /tmp/amsh_mnt             ext4      1
/dev/sdb1           /mnt/usb                  vfat      5
/tmp/secret.img     /tmp/amsh_secret          ext4      2

content.heading: technical architecture
content.text: The project is built entirely in Bash and leverages core Linux utilities. It handles signal trapping (SIGINT) to prevent accidental closures and uses `fuser` to ensure devices aren't unmounted while in use.
content.subtext: The codebase is modularized into specific components:
list: amsh.sh: The main shell loop and command processor.
mount_manager.sh: Logic for mounting, unmounting, and TTL verification.
style.sh: Handles the TUI elements, colors, and banner generation.
setup_demo.sh: A utility script that creates virtual disk images to test the functionality without physical hardware.

content.heading: logic snippet
content.text: Below is a snippet from the mount_manager.sh showing how the system checks for expired TTLs using file timestamps.
content.code:
# Check time & unmount
check_and_umount_expired() {
    if [[ ! -f "$CONFIG_FILE" ]]; then return; fi

    while read -r device mpoint fstype ttl; do
        local ttl_file="$TTL_DIR/${mpoint//\//_}.last_access"

        # Check if active mountpoint
        if [[ -f "$ttl_file" ]] && mountpoint -q "$mpoint"; then
            local last_access=$(stat -c %Y "$ttl_file")
            local current_time=$(date +%s)
            local diff=$(( (current_time - last_access) / 60 ))

            # Check expiration & active processes
            if [ "$diff" -ge "$ttl" ]; then
                if ! fuser -s "$mpoint" 2>/dev/null; then
                    echo "[SYSTEM] TTL expirat. Demontare: $mpoint"
                    sudo umount "$mpoint"
                    rm "$ttl_file"
                fi
            fi
        fi
    done < "$CONFIG_FILE"
}

content.heading: conclusion
content.text: AMSH serves as a powerful demonstration of shell scripting capabilities, process management, and Linux system administration automation. It transforms the tedious task of manual mounting into a seamless, background operation.

content.heading: technical documentation (extract)
content.text: The project is documented extensively in the official technical report. Key chapters include:
list: Problem Description: Addressing 'Workflow Friction' and 'Stale Mounts' in Linux systems.
Solution Specification: Moving from reactive to 'Just-in-Time Mounting' and proactive 'Auto-Vindecare'.
Modular Design: Separation of concerns between the Core Orchestrator (amsh.sh), Business Logic (mount_manager.sh), and UI/UX Layer (style.sh).
Implementation Details: Advanced handling of path normalization, signal trapping (SIGINT), and persistent history logging.
content.subtext: For a deep dive into the design patterns and test scenarios used, refer to the full PDF documentation.
